summary: A complete step-by-step explainer screen: you give the steps' captions and a drawing, it brings the background, the visual above or beside the caption, the progress (dots, segmented bar, numbers, vertical timeline or a scrubbed track), Back / Next / play, and shortens itself to fit any size. The step count and captions may be computed at run time, so it can end early.

steps.doc: One entry per step: {"title", "text", "short"}. title is always shown; text is the full caption; short is used when there is little room (omitted: text cut to 2 lines). Each may be a plain string or a text object over live values (textMerge, textFromFloat). With `captionIndex`, the entries are caption STATES, and need not match the step count

title.doc: The subject, a heading above everything (hidden under 170 dp tall)

count.doc: Number of steps, when it is computed at run time: an expression or a "@variable" (a resources one). Back, Next and the progress follow it, so the explainer can end early. Default: the number of `steps`

captionIndex.doc: Which entry of `steps` is shown, at run time. Default: the current step. Use with `count` for computed steps: [start, swapped, kept, finished] picked by an expression

step.doc: The step, 0-based, which every control writes. Bind a resources variable ("@at", not "@step": a variable named step hides the step() function) to compute things from it in resources. Unbound: the call keeps its own. While autoplay plays it stays where play started; read `shown`

shown.doc: Publishes the whole step on screen under this name ("@stepNow"), for the `visual` slot. A tree variable: read it inside the slot, do not declare it in resources

eased.doc: Publishes the step as a moving value under this name ("@stepEased"): it glides between steps over 0.5 s, and follows the finger with progress scrub. For morphing the visual. Same rules as `shown`

progress.doc: How progress is shown. dots: small dots and "Step N of M". bar: a segmented bar and the same text. numbers: numbered circles on a line. timeline: a vertical list of all titles, the current one expanded, each row tappable (needs a static step list). scrub: a track with stops that the finger drags, the visual follows live and the caption updates on release (static list)

tappable.doc: dots, bar, numbers: tapping a stop jumps to that step, each with a label for a screen reader; no "Step N of M" text (static step list only). timeline and scrub always are

controls.doc: buttons: Back and Next. play: also play / pause, which advances every `interval` s (no play in mono). none: for tappable, timeline or scrub

buttons.doc: icons: round arrows, down to 160 dp. labels: text Back / Next, about 200 dp at least, 300 B more

layout.doc: Where the visual goes. auto: beside the caption from 280 dp wide and 1.2 x the height, above otherwise

frame.doc: panel: the visual sits in a rounded surface (a ring in mono)

background.doc: The explainer's own background, so dark and mono looks are right on any host

playing.doc: 1 while playing; pass 1 to start playing when the document loads

loop.doc: A cycle: Next and play go from the last step to the first, and there is no end face

atEnd.doc: The last step's button: restart (Start over, or onDone's) or a dimmed Next

doneLabel.doc: Label of the last step's button

onDone.doc: Runs on the last step's button instead of going back to step 1

captionLines.doc: Lines to keep free for `text`: the longest caption at the narrowest phone width. Below that much room the short form shows

inputWhen.doc: start: the input slot shows on step 1 only (pick, then step; Start over returns to it). always: on every step, and your input must set the step back to 0 itself

visualLabel.doc: What a screen reader says for the visual

width.doc: The width it has, when it is not the whole window

visual.doc: The drawing. It gets a box of exact size: a canvas with fillMaxSize, scaled from componentWidth() / componentHeight(). It reads @stepNow / @stepEased (the names you bound), or a resources variable bound to `step`

input.doc: Something to pick before stepping, e.g. Tabs bound to a resources variable. Hidden when there is no room: the default value is then used

semantics.stateDescription: Drag to move through the steps, or tap a stop

pitfalls: Do not name your variable step: a document variable called step hides the step() function in every expression, and this component uses it. Bind "@at" or "@stage"

Three ways to read the current step. Non-autoplay: bind a resources variable to `step` and read it anywhere, in resources.variables too; that is what computed explainers need. Autoplay: `step` stays where play started, so read `shown` / `eased`, tree variables, inside the visual slot only

A tree variable (`shown`, `eased`) must not go through a param that a component turns into a local: TextChoice's index reads item 0 silently and a resources expression does not convert. Read it directly in canvas or modifier expressions, or as an arg of CellRow

Computed steps: `count` is a runtime expression ("@total + 2") and `captionIndex` picks an entry of `steps`, so `steps` lists caption STATES, each of whose title and text may be a textMerge over live values. Back, Next and the progress follow the count; it needs bar or dots (not tappable, timeline or scrub, which are one node per listed step)

loop: `eased` runs back through the middle steps when the cycle wraps. A drawing for a cycle should read `shown` and fade each stage with its own {"value": "1 - min(1, abs(@now - k))", "anim": 0.5} (CMP-28)

scrub: a touch variable cannot switch layout, so while the finger is down the title and thumb follow it (drawn on the canvas) and the wrapped caption is hidden; on release the step snaps to the nearest stop and the caption returns. `eased` follows the finger with 0.2 s of lag

controls none with scrub leaves a screen reader unable to change the step: the format has no adjust action. Keep the buttons unless the host offers another way. timeline rows and tappable stops are labelled clicks and are fine

Sizes: usable from about 160 x 120 dp (icons) and 200 wide with labels. Stacked, the caption's full text needs captionLines lines plus 90 dp left for the visual, else the short form, else the title only; the visual takes what remains and can be about 40 dp at 160 x 160, so a visual must scale itself from componentWidth() / componentHeight(). Set captionLines to the longest text's line count at the narrowest width: a longer text is cut
width and height default to the window. Inside your own padding or beside other content, pass them, or the sizes come out too large

input with inputWhen start shows on the first step only and replaces the short text when room is short; with no room it hides and the current value is used. Put anything that changes the computation there: nothing can then change under a running explanation
Mono: no play button, no motion; the drawing snaps, and the visual is the caller's: use theme colours and $if theme.mono in an inline component

The whole frame is expanded, never a pattern (texts, U7). About 6.9 KB for dots and icon buttons with four steps, plus about 90 B per text. Against that: play +830 B, numbers +310, bar +60, tappable +230, panel +210, title +180, scrub +360, input +310, timeline +1800, controls none -850; mono is about 700 B less
